question.leadin: This period of less than ten years caused its country's population to drop by nearly twenty percent.
question.text: Name this period of disease and starvation caused by infected plants that affected a constituent country of the United Kingdom from 1845 to 1852.
question.answerHtml: Irish Potato Famine (or Great Famine ; or Great Hunger ; accept Gorta Mor )
question.clue: The Baring Brothers and Company ordered shipments of corn in response to this event, but other relief efforts were stopped by Charles Trevelyan, who attributed this event to divine judgment.

swap.leadin: Eamon de Valera founded this nation's largest political party, Fianna Fail.
swap.text: Name this nation, with capital at Dublin. Its northern neighbor is still part of the United Kingdom.
swap.clue: Leaders from this country include Eamon de Valera and Patrick Pearse.

question.text: Gladstone unsuccessfully pushed for the home rule of this country first conquered by Henry VIII. The failed Easter Rising occurred in this nation, which was also home to the Battle of the Boyne.
question.clue: A civil war erupted in this country between pro and anti-treaty forces led by Michael Collins and Eamon de Valera, respectively.

swap.text: During the crisis of the Third Century Aurelian built a set of these structures around Rome. Antonius Pius and Hadrian each built one of these structures that marked the northern border of the empire.
swap.answerHtml: walls [accept Aurelian Walls; accept Severan Walls; accept Hadrian’s Wall; accept Antonine Wall]
swap.clue: Construction of Austrian towns characterized by this feature rapidly increased in the 11th century.

question.leadin: Eoin ("owen") MacNeill gave orders to halt mobilization in this event, but Patrick Pearse (peers) and Tom Clarke continued anyway.
question.text: Name this rebellion, which began with a raid on the General Post Office. Roger Casement asked for German aid for this event and was later executed for his participation.
question.answerHtml: Easter Rising [or Easter uprising or Easter Rebellion or Éirí Amach na Cásca or Éirí Amach 1916 or Aiséirí na Cásca; prompt on Easter or Easter 1916 or the Rising]
question.clue: That participant, Patrick Pearse, was part of a group that took over locations such as Boland's Bakery and Jacob's Biscuit Factory, though it was centered in the General Post Office.

swap.text: One of the highlights of Paisley's leadership in Northern Ireland was taking part in negotiations for this 1998 treaty. This treaty, which is named for a Christian holiday, ended the violent period known as "The Troubles."
swap.answerHtml: Good Friday Agreement [accept, but do NOT reveal Belfast Agreement]
swap.clue: Bertie Ahern and David Andrews were signatories of this document, which was primarily negotiated by David Trimble and John Hume.

question.leadin: This event was carried out by James Carey and other members of the Invincibles.
question.text: Name this event in which Frederick Cavindish and Thomas Henry Burke were fatally stabbed.
question.clue: It resulted in the death of a man married to Prime Minister Gladstone's niece.

swap.text: For his role in the War of Independence, Collins was appointed Minister of Finance by this Taoiseach. This man founded Fianna Fail and was later elected as the third president of Ireland.
swap.clue: This leader's American citizenship allowed him to escape execution after the Easter Rising.

question.text: This leader of the Land League gave the speech that incited the original boycott. As an MP, he convinced members of the Liberal Party to support Irish Home Rule.
question.clue: From jail, this man negotiated an agreement with William Gladstone that included concessions for land tenants called the Kilmainham Treaty.

swap.text: Forgeries falsely implicated this Irish Nationalist politician in the murders, leading to the downfall of his coalition with the Liberal party. His political career was ultimately undone by his affair with Kitty O'Shea.
swap.clue: The supposed Popish Plot would have targeted a king with this regnal name.

question.leadin: One king of this city, Sigtrygg Silkbeard, was reportedly followed by valkyries into the Battle of Clontarf, which took place outside this city.
question.text: Name this city, which was the centre of an area known as the Pale after the Norman invasion of this city's country.
question.clue: Patrick Pearse proclaimed a republic in this city during a 1916 rebellion.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about poor British governmental responses to hunger strikes.
swap.text: Margaret Thatcher pronounced this IRA member to be a "criminal" who "chose to take his own life" after he died following a 66-day hunger strike in Maze Prison.
swap.clue: Winston Churchill Boulevard in Tehran was renamed for this man, prompting the British Embassy to move their main address onto a side street.

question.leadin: Daisen Kofun, the largest example of one of these structures in Japan, is shaped like a key-hole.
question.text: Name these structures exemplified by Newgrange in Ireland. In the UK, these structures are known as barrows.
question.answerHtml: burial mounds [accept passage grave or passage tombs; accept tumuli or tumulus; accept BUT DO NOT OTHERWISE REVEAL kurgans]
question.clue: The largest "platform" example of these structures in North America is the "Monks" one in Illinois.

swap.leadin: This group assassinated Lord Mountbatten with a boat bombing.
swap.text: Name this group, who also carried out the Docklands and Manchester bombings in the 1990's. One of its members, Bobby Sands, was elected to Parliament and died in a 1981 hunger strike.
swap.answerHtml: Provisional Irish Republican Army [accept IRA, PIRA, or the Provos, do not accept “Official Irish Republican Army”]
swap.clue: While in H-Block in 1981, a member of this group on hunger strike was elected to parliament.

question.leadin: "'God save Ireland!' said the heroes / 'God save Ireland' said they all." Answer the following about Irish rebel music.
question.text: Dominic Behan's song "Come Out Ye [these people]" asks them to tell their wives "...how the IRA made you run like hell away / from the green and lovely lanes of Killeshandra." This notoriously brutal auxiliary force opened fire at a Gaelic football match at Croke Park.
question.clue: Members of this group were paid just 10 shillings per day, and most were veterans of World War I. This group killed 12 people in Croke Park at a football match in the aftermath of Bloody Sunday.

swap.text: This Provisional IRA member was elected to Parliament while imprisoned at HM Prison Maze. He died in May 1981 after leading a hunger strike in protest against the removal of the Special Category Status for IRA prisoners.
swap.clue: During Thatcher's first term, this member of the IRA led a 1981 hunger strike against Ireland's "Special Category Status." He died of starvation in the Maze Prison.

question.leadin: Settlers in this region included wealthy "Undertakers" and war veterans called "Servitors."
question.text: Name this region whose "plantation" during James I's reign began after a failed rebellion in the Nine Years' War. The "Flight of the Earls" from this region marked the end of its old order.
question.answerHtml: Ulster [or Ulaidh or Cúige Uladh or Ulstèr; accept “Plantation of Ulster”; prompt on Ireland or Éire or Airlann]
question.clue: This region was the center of the Flight of the Earls that escaped from Oriel and Tyrconnell which were both in this region.

swap.text: This younger sister of Charles Parnell led the Ladies' Land League and wrote The Tale of a Great Sham. A plaque on her tombstone carries her quote "the best part of independence; the independence of mind."
swap.answerHtml: Anna Catherine Parnell [grudgingly prompt on (A.) Parnell ]

question.leadin: Name these sources which document the extreme weather events of 535 to 536 C.E., the most significant global cooling in the past 2,000 years.
question.text: This set of annals documents the frigid weather of the 530s as well as many other severe climate events over centuries of Irish history. These annals were compiled by monks on a namesake island in the Lakes of Killarney.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about hunger strikes.
swap.text: Bobby Sands died while participating in a hunger strike in this prison. Irish nationalists carried out the Blanket Protest and the Dirty Protest in this prison that closed in 2000.
swap.clue: The "blanket" and "dirty" protests began in this facility after a group of detainees lost their political status.
